docs.title: About
docs.text: This project was for a Studio named 'Dark Tech'. Its main focus was to have us students look at the ethical side of technology and then go deeper into the negative side or dark side.

docs.title: Project theme
docs.text: The project was done in a group of 5 students and the subject my group had was themed 'The Punishing Home'. The main goal of this theme was to make an installation that would shock the user and confront them with how a smart system, in a dark tech setting, could react/handle towards the user.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text: On this page the process of the project Dark Tech can be found. The DevLog gives an overview of all the events and my work during this project, reflections on the work and the final delivered provocatype.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: "Nellie is programmed to be the perfect digital assistant. But something sinister lurks in her source code—and now she’s the perfect killer". A piece from a book called 'The Mansion' by Ezekiel Boone, that is about a smart home controlled by an AI that becomes a killer fits the project 'The Punishing Home'. The project is about testing how users might react to a smart home system turning against them based on their behavior. This is of course not the same as murder, but what would happen if a smart home system would turn itself against you even if it's just not doing some of the work it was designed to do. Would that make your life less pleasant or less livable? What if it hurt you? Would you still want to, or could you still live in a house like that? That is what will be analyzed in this short analysis, where we look at what could be the edges of uninhabitability for the implementation of a smart home system for a user's house.

docs.title: Dark value: uninhabitability
docs.text:
What is uninhabitability within the scope of this analysis? For this analysis it means to make a place, in this case a house, so uncomfortable that a user does not want to live in it. Or that the place would be a danger to their or those around their health, mental or physical and thus not safe to live in. The opposite can then be defined as a habitable place, meaning a place that would give the user the feeling of safety and comfort, something that a developer would want to create with its smart home system. A smart home system in this case is defined as an AI that controls technology in the house that perform actions like cleaning, cooking or turning the lights on/off.

When you think of a smart system, a user might buy it to make their lives or the lives of those around them easier, comfortable. But where do you stop when it comes to what technology is put in the house to create that, as too much might cause someone to feel useless or restless as they don't have anything else to do than sit or stare at a tv all day. Or what do you have it do when it comes to cooking where ingredients need to be cut or diced. Do you let the user do it or does the system also do it, but how do you provide the knives to do the cutting or dicing. These questions quickly raise a concern for how safe an environment can be.

docs.title: Needs of a user and indirect actors
docs.text:
There are a lot of different smart home systems available these days that lock a door or turn lights on/off based on someone's presence in the room. But also think about a washing machine that can be connected so it can be turned on or off remotely, or a coffee machine that knows morning routines and automatically makes a cup according to the learned pattern. All small actions that make a person's life easier and comfortable and that is exactly why a user would buy a smart home system. It would allow someone to focus on other things like their hobbies or just feeling at rest and not having to think about cleaning the house for instance.

But a user is not only the person(s) living in the house but also someone like a visitor or a pet. A visitor might not care about the washing machine that automatically turns on as its not their own. A pet might not care about the coffee being made for the person but would care about their own food. This then also sketches a pattern that shows that needs are something that is personal and that everyone has different needs that make the uninhabitability have different edges.

To make it easy to define some edges it helps to categorize the needs of users and indirect actors.

docs.title: Comfort
docs.text: Comfort is a need that everyone wants, that goes for the user and indirect actors like pets or guests. If something is comfortable it provides a pleasant feeling and does not give physical problems. Think about the temperature in a room or the brightness of the lights in a room. For instance the "comfort zone" is defined in terms of these scales of warmth.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Security is not only the feeling of being safe from a home invader, but also about health. The protection of health for a user or an individual actor like a pet are also a form of security as this is the main basis of being safe. If a system keeps the lights on in every room that the user is in it could cause the user to not be able to sleep in the home, that in turn causes discomfort and an aversion to the house.

docs.title: Efficiency
docs.text: Efficiency is something people might have as a main priority, as it can make everyday tasks easier and more convenient. For example, a video loading within one second or when you are hungry there is already something to eat. It reduces the time and effort needed to get what you want. However, efficiency is not always the main priority as some people enjoy the process of preparing their own food rather than having technology do it for them. Efficiency, for some people, can make a place more habitable, but what if this is taken to an extreme? Take the food for instance, what if you think about food and the system has already made or is making it for your. For someone that values convenience, this might be perfect, its there and you can immediately satisfy your needs. But what if this always happens, even when you are not actually hungry? This could end up wasting food or encourage unnecessary eating. It could also result in discomfort in the house, as users can not longer freely think about food without triggering the system. Now for some this might not be a problem, look at the TV and you see enough programs about overweight people that are happy in their state, but the majority of people would probably find it uncomfortable.

docs.title: Risk
docs.text: The edge when a place becomes uninhabitable is based on who is being asked but overall it could be stated that when a system gives a user or indirect actors the feeling of discomfort for prolonged time or actually hurts them and risks their physical or mental safety it is crossing the edge. But when does crossing this edge really become a risk? In the current world there are countless examples where an edge of acceptability is crossed but its still done, take the use of fossil fuel as an example. There are more environmentally friendly alternatives but they are not used that much. So applying that to a smart home system, would people be oke with a system that creates a routine based on what you have done and activates the technology in the house based on it. Say for instance, the user drinks a lot of energy drinks and the system picks this up and orders a lot of energy drinks. But when the user decides to not drink a lot there is a lot or maybe even the only thing to drink, so it forces the user to drink it. This could then be a risk but is this acceptable? From a business perspective its a good thing as the producer can sell a lot, but the user is forced to live in a place that only serves them one drink.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: In the end, it's not perfectly clear where the edge of uninhabitability for a smart system begins as this can be different from person to person. Its up to the user to decide what smart systems to implement into the house and how they allow it to control the house. Its up to the producers/developers to confine the AI to only do what the user wants it to do and not more. This then in turn defines the edge of uninhabitability as the comfort level of a person or group of individuals.

docs.title: Project
docs.text: During Dark Tech i was assigned to the project called 'Punishing Home'. This project was about letting a user(s) think about smart home systems and the dark ethical side that it can bring. The project concept was as followed: "A smart home system that punishes the user for their behavior".

docs.title: Sprint Overview
docs.text: This was the very first sprint where we as a team had to start to get to know each other and had to begin with a direction for the project. During the Sprint we made the base concept of the provocatype we wanted to work on and did an individual analysis on a topic related to the project. For me that analysis was about uninhabitability and it can be found here

docs.title: Sprint Goals
docs.text:
For this sprint the other N3 and I decided to take the lead during the project and we discussed that we should start with a design. The reason for this was that we would have to make an installation as a final provocatype and therefore needed to start with a good design to use as the base of the idea. This would help with having something solid that could be expanded with extra small things to bring the project together.

So the goal for this Sprint was to have a base to work from and to brainstorm what we could bring together in Sprint 2.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text:
To get a better understanding of the project we needed to have a meeting with the stakeholder to get an understanding of the projects goal and what they wanted to achieve with it. I planned the meeting with the stakeholder and checked when they and the team had time. Luckily the meeting was able to be planned during the first half of the sprint.

After having a better understanding of what we needed to deliver the other N3 and me started with individual drawings so we could come together and pickout parts we loved from each drawing to then continue on to making a small prototype in 2 groups. But starting with individual drawings could result in to big of a difference in what needed to be done so we started with a brainstorm session and a mood board, so we would be more on the same line but still be able to have individual idea's.

docs.title: Research & Exploration
docs.text: When we started we had no vision on what the project was about and what it had to accomplish but after talking with the stakeholder we got a better understanding. During the meeting the other N3 and me took the lead. We where the main speakers to get a better understanding for the project as we had more experience in doing so. In the meeting I made sure to keep track of the time as we only had about 15-20 minutes but had a lot of questions. To ensure we would have a decent understanding of the project i filtered out the questions we had made in advance to once that would achieve this result. In the end we did mis some questions that would help us understand the project a little bit more the we already had so I decided we should send those with the debriefing to the stakeholder to still get an answer on them, and we did.

docs.title: Initial Research
docs.text:
During the Brainstorm and mood board session i had a difficult time to come with ideas as I could not place my self in the correct mindset. It took me a bit to feel some creativity but the others came with ideas and this helped with me being able to feel more ideas coming up. During the brainstorm we came to a collective decision to start with a living room and have the experience within that room.

After the mood board we split up and went on to create individual ideas. But during that time we also had to do an individual analysis on a topic related to the project where mine was about uninhabitability. To read that analysis go to this page.

Because i had an angle of uninhabitability I tried to look at how the experience could make someone uncomfortable and used what i had already researched to do so. docs.title: Design Process
docs.text: After having made the individual drawings we came together to discuss what we had made and look at what could be used in the provocatype. From my drawing we decided to go for the flow of the experience and how we could make the user feel uncomfortable. Then we split up where i made the decision to split in groups where each had a N3 student, so that resulted in me being paired with another team member and the other N3 as well.
